commands.summary: Print the current working directory

options.description: Use the logical path from the environment, including symbolic links.
Resolve symbolic links in the printed path.

sections.heading: Description
sections.body: Prints the absolute name of the current working directory.

sections.heading: Safety
sections.body: Reads process and filesystem path information without modifying it.

commands.summary: Create hard or symbolic links

arguments.label: TARGET
arguments.description: Existing path that the link should reference.

arguments.label: LINK_NAME
arguments.description: Path of the link to create.

options.description: Create a symbolic link instead of a hard link.
With symbolic, make the link target relative to the link location.
Remove an existing destination before creating the link.
Prompt before removing an existing destination.
Treat a destination symlink to a directory as a normal file.

sections.heading: Description
sections.body: Creates a hard link by default or a symbolic link when requested.

sections.heading: Risk
sections.body: Creates directory entries and force mode can replace an existing destination.

commands.summary: Print a symbolic link target or canonical path

arguments.label: FILE
arguments.description: Symbolic links or paths to inspect.

options.description: Canonicalize by following every symlink; all but the final component must exist.
Canonicalize only when every path component exists.
Canonicalize without requiring any path component to exist.
Do not output a trailing delimiter.
End each output with NUL instead of newline.

sections.heading: Description
sections.body: Prints symbolic-link values or canonicalized path names.

sections.heading: Safety
sections.body: Inspects path metadata without changing links or targets.

commands.summary: Resolve and print absolute path names

arguments.label: FILE
arguments.description: Paths to resolve.

options.description: Require every component of the path to exist.
Resolve path components without requiring them to exist.
Resolve parent references before symbolic links.
Resolve symbolic links before parent references.
Print paths relative to the selected directory.

sections.heading: Description
sections.body: Expands path names into canonical absolute or requested relative forms.

sections.heading: Safety
sections.body: Resolves path information without modifying filesystem objects.

commands.summary: Strip directory and suffix from path names

arguments.label: NAME
arguments.description: Path names to reduce to their final component.

options.description: Accept multiple path-name arguments.
Remove the specified trailing suffix.
End each output with NUL instead of newline.

sections.heading: Description
sections.body: Prints the final component of each path after optional suffix removal.

sections.heading: Safety
sections.body: Transforms path text without accessing or changing the named files.

commands.summary: Strip the final component from path names

arguments.label: NAME
arguments.description: Path names whose directory components should be printed.

options.description: End each output with NUL instead of newline.

sections.heading: Description
sections.body: Prints each path with its final slash-delimited component removed.

sections.heading: Safety
sections.body: Transforms path text without modifying filesystem objects.

commands.summary: Select bytes, characters, or fields from input lines

arguments.label: FILE
arguments.description: Input files; standard input is used when omitted.

options.description: Select only the specified byte ranges.
Select only the specified character ranges.
Select only the specified field ranges.
Use the selected input field delimiter instead of TAB.
Do not print lines that contain no delimiter.

sections.heading: Description
sections.body: Writes selected portions of each input line to standard output.

sections.heading: Safety
sections.body: Reads input without modifying it.

commands.summary: Translate, squeeze, or delete characters

arguments.label: SET1
arguments.description: Input character set.

arguments.label: SET2
arguments.description: Replacement or squeeze character set.

options.description: Use the complement of the first character set.
Delete characters in the first set instead of translating them.
Replace each repeated character run with one occurrence.
Truncate the first set to the length of the second set.

sections.heading: Description
sections.body: Transforms characters read from standard input and writes the result to standard output.

sections.heading: Safety
sections.body: Does not modify files unless the surrounding shell redirects its output.

commands.summary: Report or omit adjacent repeated lines

arguments.label: INPUT
arguments.description: Input file; standard input is used when omitted.

arguments.label: OUTPUT
arguments.description: Optional file to receive the result.

options.description: Prefix each line with its occurrence count.
Print only duplicated line groups.
Print only lines that are not repeated.
Ignore case differences when comparing lines.
Ignore the specified number of leading fields.

sections.heading: Description
sections.body: Compares adjacent lines and prints selected duplicate or unique groups.

sections.heading: Risk
sections.body: Supplying OUTPUT writes a file; omit it for a read-only standard-output operation.

commands.summary: Copy standard input to files and standard output

arguments.label: FILE
arguments.description: Files that should receive a copy of standard input.

options.description: Append to files instead of overwriting them.
Ignore interrupt signals.

sections.heading: Description
sections.body: Copies standard input to standard output and to every selected file.

sections.heading: Risk
sections.body: Overwrites selected files by default or appends when requested.

commands.summary: Build and execute command lines from standard input

arguments.label: COMMAND
arguments.description: Command to execute; echo is used when omitted.

arguments.label: ARGUMENT
arguments.description: Arguments placed before values read from standard input.

options.description: Read NUL-delimited items and treat every character literally.
Use at most the specified number of input items per invocation.
Run up to the specified number of processes concurrently.
Replace occurrences of a token in initial arguments with each input line.
Do not execute the command when standard input has no items.

sections.heading: Description
sections.body: Reads items from standard input and invokes a command with those items as arguments.

sections.heading: Risk
sections.body: Executes another command, possibly many times or concurrently; review delimiters and the complete delegated command.

commands.summary: Find path names using a file-name database

arguments.label: PATTERN
arguments.description: Name or path patterns to find in the locate database.

options.description: Match only the final path component.
Print only the number of matches.
Match patterns without regard to case.
Stop after the specified number of matches.
Print only paths that still exist when they are checked.

sections.heading: Description
sections.body: Searches a periodically updated file-name database and prints matching paths.

sections.heading: Freshness
sections.body: Results reflect the database snapshot and may include removed paths or omit newly created paths.

commands.summary: Find process IDs by name and attributes

arguments.label: PATTERN
arguments.description: Regular expression matched against process names or command lines.

options.description: Match against the complete command line.
Require the process name or command line to match exactly.
Select only the most recently started match.
Select only the least recently started match.
Match processes whose effective user ID is in the list.

sections.heading: Description
sections.body: Searches running processes and prints identifiers that satisfy all selected criteria.

sections.heading: Matching
sections.body: Name matching is limited unless full command-line matching is selected.

commands.summary: Signal processes selected by name and attributes

arguments.label: PATTERN
arguments.description: Regular expression used to select processes.

options.description: Send the selected signal instead of SIGTERM.
Match against the complete command line.
Require an exact process-name or command-line match.
Signal only the most recently started match.
Signal only the least recently started match.
Match processes whose effective user ID is in the list.

sections.heading: Description
sections.body: Selects processes by name and attributes and sends each one a signal.

sections.heading: Risk
sections.body: A broad or incorrect pattern can interrupt multiple unrelated processes.

commands.summary: Display a live view of processes and system load

options.description: Write non-interactive output suitable for redirection.
Exit after the specified number of updates.
Wait the specified number of seconds between updates.
Monitor only the selected comma-separated process IDs.
Show only processes with the selected effective user.

sections.heading: Description
sections.body: Displays a continuously updated process list and system summary.

sections.heading: Lifecycle
sections.body: Interactive mode remains active until quit; batch mode should use a bounded iteration count when appropriate.

commands.summary: Inspect or change the system host name

arguments.label: COMMAND
arguments.description: Operation such as status or hostname.

arguments.label: NAME
arguments.description: Host name supplied to a changing operation.

options.description: Operate on the static host name.
Operate on the transient host name.
Operate on the descriptive pretty host name.
Do not prompt for authentication.

sections.heading: Description
sections.body: Queries system host-name metadata or requests a host-name change through systemd.

sections.heading: Risk
sections.body: Changing a host name affects system identity and generally requires authorization.

commands.summary: Inspect or change system time settings

arguments.label: COMMAND
arguments.description: Operation such as status, set-timezone, or set-ntp.

arguments.label: VALUE
arguments.description: Value supplied to the selected operation.

options.description: Do not prompt for authentication.
Synchronize the system clock when changing local-RTC mode.

sections.heading: Description
sections.body: Queries or controls system time, time zone, RTC, and network-time synchronization settings.

sections.heading: Risk
sections.body: Changing clocks or time zones affects timestamps, schedules, authentication, and distributed services.

commands.summary: Inspect or control login sessions and users

arguments.label: COMMAND
arguments.description: Operation such as list-sessions, show-user, or terminate-session.

arguments.label: NAME
arguments.description: Session, user, or seat identifiers.

options.description: Show only the selected property; may be repeated.
Print property values without names.
Show properties even when they are unset.
Do not send output through a pager.
Do not prompt for authentication.

sections.heading: Description
sections.body: Introspects and controls systemd login sessions, users, and seats.

sections.heading: Risk
sections.body: Control operations can terminate sessions or signal all processes belonging to a user.

commands.summary: Print block-device content attributes

arguments.label: DEVICE
arguments.description: Block devices to inspect.

options.description: Use the selected output format.
Show only the selected tag; may be repeated.
Search for a device with the selected NAME=value token.
Use low-level superblock probing mode.
Look up the device that has the selected UUID.

sections.heading: Description
sections.body: Reads filesystem, swap, RAID, and partition metadata from block devices or a cache.

sections.heading: Safety
sections.body: Inspection does not alter device contents, though direct probing may require privileges.

commands.summary: List or find mounted filesystems

arguments.label: DEVICE|MOUNTPOINT
arguments.description: Optional device or mount point to find.

options.description: Produce JSON output.
Use list output instead of a tree.
Do not print column headings.
Select a comma-separated list of output columns.
Search for a filesystem by source.
Show the filesystem containing the selected path.
Limit results to the selected filesystem types.

sections.heading: Description
sections.body: Lists mounted filesystems or searches mount and fstab data by source or target.

sections.heading: Scripting
sections.body: Select explicit output columns because the default human-readable output can change.

commands.summary: Detach filesystems from the directory tree

arguments.label: DIRECTORY|DEVICE
arguments.description: Mounted directories or devices to detach.

options.description: Unmount eligible filesystems from the mount table.
Force unmounting, primarily for an unreachable network filesystem.
Detach now and clean references after they are no longer busy.
Recursively unmount nested mounts below each selected directory.
Operate only on the selected comma-separated filesystem types.
Report operations verbosely.

sections.heading: Description
sections.body: Detaches selected filesystems from the visible directory hierarchy.

sections.heading: Risk
sections.body: Unmounting can disrupt applications, make files unavailable, or lose buffered work; recursive, forced, and lazy modes need extra review.

commands.summary: Download files from network URLs

arguments.label: URL
arguments.description: HTTP, HTTPS, or FTP resources to retrieve.

options.description: Write all retrieved content to the selected file.
Continue a partially downloaded file.
Suppress normal output.
Follow links and retrieve resources recursively.
Do not overwrite files that already exist.
Limit retrieval attempts to the selected count.

sections.heading: Description
sections.body: Retrieves resources over supported network protocols and normally stores them as local files.

sections.heading: Risk
sections.body: Creates or replaces files and downloads untrusted network content; recursive retrieval can be large.

commands.summary: Compress or decompress files in the xz format

arguments.label: FILE
arguments.description: Files to compress or decompress.

options.description: Compress input files; this is the default operation.
Decompress input files.
Keep input files after successful processing.
Overwrite output files and process additional input types.
Write output to standard output and keep input files.
Use up to the selected number of worker threads.

sections.heading: Description
sections.body: Compresses files to xz format or restores compressed input.

sections.heading: Risk
sections.body: Successful processing normally replaces input files unless keep or standard-output mode is selected.

commands.summary: Build targets by executing makefile recipes

arguments.label: TARGET|NAME=VALUE
arguments.description: Build goals and command-line variable assignments.

options.description: Change to the selected directory before reading makefiles.
Read build rules from the selected file.
Run up to the selected number of recipes concurrently.
Print recipes without executing most of them.
Treat all targets as out of date.

sections.heading: Description
sections.body: Reads dependency rules and executes recipes needed to update selected targets.

sections.heading: Risk
sections.body: Makefile recipes are executable commands and may change files, services, networks, or external systems.
